title: Full CI runs on heads that autosquash will delete
description:
Every batch pays two or three full CI runs where one would do. The review cycle pushes a fixup after the code-review pass, then another after the simplify pass, then collapses both with 'git rebase --autosquash' and force-pushes. Only the final head can merge; the intermediate ones are rewritten out of existence. Measured on PR #83: three CI runs at ~3.5 minutes each on backend, frontend, both container images, the compose stack and the browser suite, of which two were on heads that no longer exist.

WHY THE MECHANISM ALREADY THERE DOES NOT CATCH IT. ci.yml:11 already sets a concurrency group of workflow+ref with cancel-in-progress: true, and it is correct -- a pull_request run uses refs/pull/N/merge, so both pushes share a group. It cannot help here because it can only cancel a run that is still in flight, and the runs are not: CI finishes in ~3.5 minutes while a review or simplify pass takes fifteen or more. The pushes never overlap, so nothing is ever cancelled. On PR #83 the three runs were 20 minutes and 2 hours apart.

THE PROPERTY THAT IS DETERMINISTIC. A head carrying a 'fixup!' commit provably cannot be the head that merges, because --autosquash rewrites it first. That is checkable from the commit range alone, needs no instruction anybody has to remember, and is exactly the class of head whose expensive jobs are wasted.

WHAT MAKES IT NOT A ONE-LINER, AND WHY THIS IS A DECISION RATHER THAN A CLEANUP:

1. It must not become a failure. check-batch.sh --unfinished deliberately downgrades 'commits waiting to be folded in' from a failure to a note, and ci.yml:736 records why: as --draft the job failed on 48% of all pull request runs, and the failure was the process doing what it is told. inventory-tng-ee2c is that decision. Failing a fixup-carrying head reverses it.

2. It must not become green either. scripts/repo-settings.sh:47 derives the required contexts from every job name in ci.yml, so each expensive job is required by existing and being named -- the property inventory-tng-x0jp was built on. A job skipped by an 'if:' reports its check run as 'skipped', which satisfies a required status check. So the naive fix -- skip the expensive jobs when the range holds a fixup! -- would make a fixup-carrying head look GREEN and mergeable on GitHub's side, which is the direction docs/decisions/0020-who-merges.md exists to refuse.

So the shape that satisfies both is an aggregate required context: the expensive jobs stop being required individually, one cheap job needs: them all and reports failure unless each dependency succeeded, and skipping a dependency is therefore red rather than green. That changes what a required context IS in this repository, which is why it wants a docs/decisions entry and not a patch: it touches the derivation in repo-settings.sh, the contexts on main, and the property x0jp leaned on.

VERIFY BEFORE BUILDING: that a skipped required context really does satisfy branch protection under this repository's settings, rather than being assumed from the general GitHub behaviour.

Found while landing PR #83.

title: Both review stages are satisfiable without a review pass
description:
review_cycle.BY_REVIEW accepts ANY entry under `reviews` as evidence for the
code-review stage, deliberately -- an inline diff comment arrives as an entry
with an empty body, and that is a review pass leaving evidence.

But a reply to a review thread also creates one, and .agents/skills/pull-
requests/SKILL.md instructs exactly that when answering findings. So an agent
following the documented procedure can satisfy code-review by replying to a
thread, and simplify by posting its own findings comment, having never had a
review pass run at all.

NOT NEW. The gate accepted the same evidence, and docs/decisions/0020-who-
merges.md has always said a gate can make forgetting hard and cannot make lying
hard. What changed is that this now decides a required check, so the failure is
a merge nobody reviewed rather than a receipt nobody trusts.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY DISCRIMINATE, and none of it is free: a review whose state
is not COMMENTED; a review by an actor other than the pull request author; a
review carrying at least one inline comment or a non-empty body. The second is
the strongest and the most likely to be wrong for this project, which has one
active maintainer who is usually also the author. That is why this is filed as
a question rather than a fix.

Related: inventory-tng-8nqo, on what makes a review current enough to count.
close_reason: Closed

title: carries() counts a marker inside a nested fence
description:
The fence toggle in scripts/review_cycle.py treats every line beginning ``` or
~~~ as a delimiter, ignoring nesting and fence length. Verified by execution:

  outer ```` fence, inner ``` fence, marker between  -> counted as POSTED
  outer ~~~ fence, inner ``` fence, marker between   -> counted as POSTED
  plain ``` fence                                    -> correctly not posted
  a marker preceded by a TAB                         -> counted as POSTED

That is the inventory-tng-egh4.1 failure one nesting level up, and the way
somebody would hit it is ordinary rather than adversarial: showing a fenced
block requires wrapping it in a longer fence, and .agents/skills/pull-requests/
SKILL.md displays the marker inside a fence. Quote that section in a comment
and the comment becomes evidence that the pass ran.

The tab case is the same class: the reader counts a tab as one character where
Markdown renders it as a code block, so a marker Markdown is DISPLAYING is read
as one that was POSTED.

PRE-EXISTING -- it came over unchanged from the gate -- but its blast radius is
now branch protection rather than one machine's hook, which is why it is filed
at P2 rather than left.

THE FIX IS A REAL PARSER FOR THIS ONE RULE: track the opening fence's character
and length, close only on a fence of the same character and at least that
length, and expand a leading tab before measuring the indent. Both halves want
cases in scripts/review-cycle.test.sh, which already has the shapes to copy.
close_reason: Closed

title: The stop hook asks for a simplify pass that has already run
description:
Seen on PR #81 the moment inventory-tng-d854 landed its message, which makes
it the same defect surviving one file over.

WHAT HAPPENS. The agent runs /simplify, posts the findings with the marker, and
asks for /code-review because it cannot run that one. The Stop hook then says:

  missing: code-review  ask a person to run: /code-review 81 --comment
           simplify     yours to run: /simplify

The second line is false. The pass ran, and its evidence is on the pull request
where `marked()` would find it.

WHY. `stop_mode` reads `receipt_status`, which reads .claude/.review-receipts.json
and nothing else -- it never asks GitHub. And `record_receipt` exits 1 BEFORE
`path = os.environ["RECEIPTS"]` whenever any stage is unevidenced, so a half-run
cycle writes no receipt at all. No receipt means no evidence for any stage, so
the stop message lists both, whatever the pull request actually carries.

NOT A REGRESSION, which is why d854 shipped over it. The same state printed
"missing: code-review and simplify" before, equally wrong. What changed is that
the message is now an imperative, so being wrong costs an agent a wasted pass
rather than a moment's confusion.

THE FIX IS A CONTRACT CHANGE AND WANTS ITS OWN REVIEW. `record` would write
what it found even while refusing -- exit 1 as now, but leave a receipt
recording the stages that ARE evidenced. Then the stop message names only what
is genuinely outstanding.

MERGING IS ALREADY SAFE FOR THIS, checked rather than assumed. The merge guard
treats a receipt as its head AND its evidence, and its comment says it prints
nothing for one with a head and no evidence behind it, falling into the same
refusal -- written for precisely the partial shapes an older gate left on disk.
So a partial receipt cannot unblock a merge; it can only make the stop message
honest.

WHAT TO WATCH. The receipt stops being "the cycle ran" and becomes "here is what
has been seen so far", which is a different thing to name in DEVELOPERS.md, and
`landing-gate.test.sh` has cases resting on the old all-or-nothing shape.
close_reason: record keeps what it found even while refusing, so the stop hook names only what is outstanding; the merge guard is unchanged and still all-or-nothing.

title: The skill tells an agent to run a command only a person can run
description:
The pull-requests skill tells an agent to run two commands as steps of one
procedure. One of them an agent cannot run, and nothing in this repository says
so, so the agent improvises at the point it discovers this -- which on PR #80
meant stopping a green, finished batch and handing it back.

MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED, 2026-08-31.

* `/code-review` is refused: `Skill code-review cannot be used with Skill tool
  due to disable-model-invocation`. It is a built-in, not a repository skill --
  there is no .claude/skills/code-review here. The plugin-marketplace copy at
  plugins/code-review/commands/code-review.md carries
  `disable-model-invocation: false`, but that plugin is not enabled, so it is
  not the one in play. No change to this repository can lift the refusal.
* `/simplify` IS invocable by an agent. Confirmed by invoking it.

WHAT THE SKILL SAYS NOW. SKILL.md line 36 prints `/code-review <pr> --comment`
and line 85 prints `/simplify`, in the same voice, in a procedure the agent is
executing. A reader has no way to tell that the first is a request to make of a
person and the second is work to do.

WHAT THE STOP HOOK SAYS NOW. `missing: code-review and simplify`, with both
stages named identically. It arrives at exactly the moment the distinction
matters and does not draw it.

THE FIX IS IN THREE PLACES, and the split between them is rule 1.

1. DEVELOPERS.md "One review pass" owns the FACT: which stage an agent may run
   and which has to be asked for. One or two sentences, no procedure.
2. .agents/skills/pull-requests/SKILL.md owns the PROCEDURE: run `/simplify`
   yourself; for the review pass, ask the person, in these words, and treat the
   handoff as a step rather than a failure. It must also say plainly that
   posting `<!-- review-cycle: code-review -->` by hand, having not run the
   pass, is forgery -- landing-gate.sh's own reader already calls that out and
   the skill should agree with it.
3. scripts/landing-gate.sh names the operator per stage in the stop message,
   so the guidance arrives where the agent is standing:
   `missing: code-review (ask the person to run /code-review <pr> --comment)
   and simplify (yours to run)`.

WHY IT IS WORTH DOING RATHER THAN REMEMBERING. The cost is not the pause. It is
that an agent meeting an instruction it cannot follow will invent a way through,
and the two available inventions here are both bad: stop a finished batch, or
hand-write the marker and merge on a receipt that says a pass ran when it did
not. The second is worse and nothing structural prevents it.
close_reason: DEVELOPERS.md owns which stage has which operator; the skill owns asking for one and running the other; the gate names both in the refusal.

title: bd import silently drops defer_until
description:
Found while fixing inventory-tng-wjkd, and separate from it: bd import does not preserve defer_until.

Reproduce: take a committed export containing a bead with defer_until set, import it into a fresh workspace, export again. The field comes back null.

Measured on 2026-08-31 against this repository's own export, in a CI runner building a tracker from .beads/issues.jsonl:

  inventory-tng-61b  2027-01-05T00:00:00Z -> null
  inventory-tng-9u8  2027-02-01T00:00:00Z -> null
  inventory-tng-f8g  2026-11-01T00:00:00Z -> null

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE WORKFLOW. The export is the only thing shared between clones -- the Dolt database is gitignored -- so importing it is how any fresh clone, any new contributor, and any CI job gets a tracker. All of them lose deferrals, and the loss is silent and looks like the bead was simply never deferred. Three beads deferred to 2026-11, 2027-01 and 2027-02 would reappear in bd ready immediately.

WHAT TO DO. Report it upstream to beads, since nothing here can fix an import. Meanwhile the workflow no longer proposes an export it built by importing, which removes the only automated path by which the loss could reach main -- but a person running bd import by hand on a fresh clone still loses them, and that is worth knowing before somebody does.

Worth checking whether other fields go the same way. defer_until was found because three beads happened to carry it and the diff was small enough to read; a field no bead currently uses would not have shown up at all.

title: Run bd outside the checkout, so nothing needs undoing
description:
Flagged twice during the issue-sync work and deferred twice on scope, with a threshold set for when to stop deferring. The threshold has nearly been reached.

THE PROBLEM. The workflow runs bd inside the checkout, so bd scaffolds the checkout: bd init rewrites its hooks and config, sets core.hooksPath, and without --skip-agents appends to AGENTS.md and rewrites .claude/settings.json. It also STAGES what it rewrites. None of that is bd misbehaving -- it is bd setting up a workspace, which is what it was asked to do -- but the workspace it is setting up is a git checkout whose contents are about to be committed.

The current answer is to undo it afterwards: --skip-agents, then a hard reset, then git clean, then put the export back, then unset core.hooksPath. Five operations to unmake something that did not need making.

FOUR DEFECTS TRACE TO THIS, all in inventory-tng-cwpa.3's workflow and all found by running it rather than reading it:

- inventory-tng-65ij: bd init tried to clone the committed sync remote over SSH, because the checkout carries .beads/config.yaml.
- inventory-tng-rbvb: the proposed commit held ten files including eighty new lines on AGENTS.md, because bd scaffolded and its hooks staged.
- inventory-tng-y466: the restore used a working-tree checkout, which takes content from the index, so it faithfully restored what bd had staged.
- and inventory-tng-t3w9 is only adjacent -- an install problem rather than a workspace one -- but it is a fourth thing that had to be discovered by merging an unverifiable job.

THE STRUCTURAL FIX. Run bd in a directory of its own, outside the working tree, and let the checkout hold nothing but the export. Copy .beads/issues.jsonl into a scratch directory, init and import and sync there, export back into the checkout, commit. The checkout is then never scaffolded, never staged into, and needs no undoing -- and the restore, the clean, the hooks-path unset and --skip-agents all become unnecessary rather than load-bearing.

WHY IT WAS NOT DONE ALREADY, so the deferral is judged rather than assumed. scripts/pull-new-issues.sh derives the export path from the git root, so bd running elsewhere needs that path to be overridable -- an interface change to a script with fourteen test cases, made in service of a workflow detail, at a moment when the workflow was still failing for unrelated reasons. Undoing the scaffolding was four lines and no interface change. That was the right call twice and it stops being the right call the moment a fifth defect appears.

WHAT TO DO. Give pull-new-issues.sh an export path override -- an argument or an environment variable, with the current behaviour as the default so nothing else changes -- and have the workflow run bd with its workspace in RUNNER_TEMP. Then delete the restore, the clean, the config move, the hooks-path unset and --skip-agents, and check the proposed commit still holds exactly one file.

THE TEST THAT MUST SURVIVE. Whatever shape this takes, the property worth keeping is the one the current arrangement stumbled into: the job prints a short git status after touching the checkout. That single line is what turned inventory-tng-y466 from several runs of guessing into one, and any rewrite that drops it is trading a real diagnostic for tidiness.

title: Require enrolment of new devices only, and grandfather the rest
description:
The project owner, 2026-08-31: 'is there a way to do a per user requirement for the enrollment and request signing? that way it would allow us to keep working with demo users and also allow the sign up flow to be tested by new user'.

IT CANNOT BE PER USER, AND DOES NOT NEED TO BE. Volunteers have no accounts (decision 0012 point 3), so at the moment a gate must decide, the only identity a request carries is the device token. There is no user yet -- the volunteer is picked from the list AFTER the app answers.

PER DEVICE GIVES BOTH THINGS ASKED FOR. Device already carries what this needs: identifier, enrolled_at (auto_now_add), enrolled_from, revoked_at. A cutoff on enrolled_at grandfathers every device already in use, so demo users notice nothing, while a device with no token meets the enrolment flow and the sign-up path gets exercised by real new users.

NO CRYPTOGRAPHY. The token is already minted and signed with django.core.signing -- AGENTS.md rule 3, route 1, an established library already carrying this project's threat model. The gate is a permission class reading presented_device(): DEVICE_ENROLLED before the cutoff passes, NO_DEVICE is sent to enrolment. Minting is what starts asking for a code. inventory-tng-jro is the separate and much larger question of registered keys and signed requests, and this issue must not drift into it.

THE THING THAT MUST BE WRITTEN DOWN RATHER THAN LEARNED LATER. While any ungated path remains, this buys TESTING CONVENIENCE AND NOT SECURITY. Anybody can still mint a token; DeviceEnrolmentView answers everybody by design and its own docstring says the guard is the throttle rather than the signature. The same trap the demo brief's act four describes. The security arrives on the day the old path closes and not before, so the announcement, the docs and the setting's own module must say so, or the first person to see 'enrolment required' will conclude the problem is solved.

DEPENDS ON inventory-tng-2jzx. If the network does admission -- and on 2026-08-31 the owner confirmed that rooftop volunteers demonstrably DO WireGuard into the mesh rather than merely that they can, which removes the exclusion that made a network posture look unusable -- then an application-level gate is defence in depth rather than the control, and its priority drops. Settle that first.

WHAT THAT CONFIRMATION DID NOT REACH, and it is the half this issue turns on. The VPN carries a request to the application; it hands nobody a code, so it does not answer enrolled_code at all. Being reachable is not being identified, and this issue is about the second. So the confirmation is not on its own an argument for dropping this. 2jzx's note of that date holds the evidence and the other limit.

title: Pull on a schedule, and open a pull request rather than push
description:
Phase 3, which is what makes 'kept up to date when other users add issues' true for issues nobody local has heard of.

A GitHub Action, on issues events and on a schedule, that bootstraps beads from the committed export, runs phase 1's discovery, and proposes the result.

A PULL REQUEST RATHER THAN A COMMIT TO MAIN, for three reasons all verified rather than supposed:

1. scripts/check-commit.sh demands a Closes: or Refs: trailer and exempts only a merge, a revert and a cherry-pick. A bot commit carrying tracker state closes nothing and would be refused.
2. .beads/issues.jsonl is a megabyte on one line per issue. A bot committing to main while somebody has local tracker changes is a conflict nobody wants to resolve by hand.
3. An issue somebody else filed should be SEEN arriving. A pull request puts it in front of a person, which is where phase 4 happens anyway.

CI has no Dolt database -- it is gitignored -- so the job restores from .beads/issues.jsonl first. Confirm bd bootstrap or bd import is the right entry point and that it does not need a Dolt server in a runner.

Guard the loop: a job that commits the export must not trigger itself. Use the standard paths-ignore or a bot-actor check, and say which in the workflow.

title: Push what reaches origin, from the pre-push hook
description:
Phase 2. Beads already installs a pre-push hook; this adds the push half of the sync to it, so state that reaches origin reaches the issue list without anybody remembering.

ORDER MATTERS AND IS THE POINT. Discover and pull first (phase 1), then look, then push:

  1. discovery script -> bd github pull <new numbers>
  2. bd github sync --pull-only        # refresh the ones already linked
  3. git diff --stat .beads/issues.jsonl
  4. bd github sync --push-only

Step 3 is the defensiveness the owner asked for. With --prefer-newer an incoming GitHub edit can replace a bead's description, and because the export is committed that arrives as a reviewable diff before anything leaves the machine. 'git checkout .beads/issues.jsonl' undoes it.

A hook that pushes must not block a git push when GitHub is unreachable or the token is absent. Warn and carry on -- the tracker is not made wrong by a failed sync, and a hook that strands somebody offline will be disabled by the first person it strands.

Needs a token in the environment. Say in DEVELOPERS.md where it comes from and that a contributor without one is not broken, only unsynced.
notes:
=== BUILT AS A COMMAND, NOT A PRE-PUSH HOOK, 2026-08-31 ===

This issue asked for the push half to run from the pre-push hook. Building it showed that to be the wrong place, so it is a script instead and cwpa.3 carries the automation. Recorded here rather than diverged from quietly.

WHAT DECIDED IT, measured rather than reasoned: pushing writes external_ref onto every bead it files an issue for, which rewrites .beads/issues.jsonl. Checked by pushing one bead and diffing the export before and after. So a hook on git push would leave the tracker dirty the instant the push finished -- uncommitted, unnoticed, and exactly the way tracker state gets stranded and lost. The stored memory about staging .beads with the next batch is about that failure already happening by hand; automating it would make it happen every push.

Two lesser reasons, either of which would be worth weighing and neither of which decides it alone: every contributor would need a GitHub token to push code, and every push would wait on the GitHub API for the benefit of promptness alone.

WHERE IT WENT INSTEAD. scripts/sync-issues.sh runs the four steps in the safe order -- discover and pull, refresh what is linked, SHOW WHAT ARRIVED, then push -- and a person runs it when they want it. cwpa.3 runs the same script in CI, where the export change is committed in the pull request it opens rather than abandoned in somebody's working tree.

The ordering argument this issue made is unchanged and is now in the script's header: --prefer-newer is safe here because the export is committed, so an incoming edit is a reviewable diff and git checkout undoes it. Pulling first and looking is what turns that from a property into a practice.

title: EPIC: GitHub issues and beads, synced both ways
description:
The project owner, 2026-08-31: a two-way sync, kept up to date when other users add issues in either place, with --prefer-newer while it is still unknown whether people will use beads.

WHAT WAS MEASURED ON 2026-08-31, so nobody re-derives it. One bead was pushed and a throwaway round-tripped; both GitHub test issues were deleted afterwards and the tracker was left clean.

WORKS ALREADY:
- bd github sync/push/pull/status exist. Configure with GITHUB_TOKEN and GITHUB_REPOSITORY in the environment, or bd config; nothing was committed to .beads/config.yaml.
- The mapping is external_ref on the bead, and it SURVIVES INTO .beads/issues.jsonl. Since that file is committed, the mapping reaches every clone. This was the architectural question and it came back favourably.
- Idempotent: a second run reported 369 create and 1 update. It will not duplicate what it has already pushed.
- Push carries title, description, type::* and priority::* labels, and any labels the bead already has.
- Pull PRESERVES the fields GitHub cannot represent. A GitHub edit overwrote title and description and left acceptance_criteria, notes, priority and issue_type untouched. No silent data loss.
- Bidirectional sync pulls before it pushes, which is the order this epic wants.

DOES NOT WORK:
- PULL DOES NOT DISCOVER. A contributor opened issue #62 and 'bd github sync --pull-only' found nothing. Only 'bd github pull 62' worked, and only with a bare number -- '#62' and the full URL are both rejected by strconv.Atoi. Something must enumerate GitHub and hand bd the numbers, which is phase 1 and the whole reason this is an epic rather than a config change.
- Push is lossy in the other direction: design, acceptance_criteria, notes and every dependency are dropped. A GitHub reader sees the description only.
- A GitHub-born issue becomes a synthetic id such as inventory-tng-1788173271772-1-17c29583, typed task at priority 2. That needs a human, which is phase 4.
- There is no stored config default for the conflict strategy. It is per-invocation, so the ordering has to live in whatever hook or script runs it or it will not be followed.

WHY --prefer-newer IS SAFE ENOUGH HERE, which is the owner's choice and worth recording rather than re-arguing: issues.jsonl is committed, so an incoming GitHub edit arrives as a reviewable git diff and 'git checkout .beads/issues.jsonl' undoes it completely. The tracker has version history. The protection is the diff, not the flag.

title: Record that the tracker is public, and what may never go in a bead
description:
The project owner, 2026-08-31, on a plan to keep sensitive beads out of a GitHub mirror with a label: 'isn't using tags to hide sensitive stuff just security by obscurity? Anyone can fork the repo and go through the beads'.

Correct, and checked: .beads/issues.jsonl is tracked in a public repository, a megabyte of it, browsable, first committed 2026-08-18 and touched by 195 commits. The label would have decided what appears in an issue LIST while changing nothing about what is readable.

The owner chose to keep it public deliberately rather than withdraw it. This records that, and states the four things that must never enter a bead, since the history cannot be recalled.
