whether the TCP keepalive and statement timeouts in play bound it, or whether
this reintroduces the pinned worker 39ng removed by a different route. Measure
before choosing. If it lands, docs/deployment.md#health-checks and .env.sample
are where it is written up, beside the bound 39ng added.

title: A shared walk over urlpatterns, asserting each route answers its own URL
description:
Found by the code review of PR #25 (inventory-tng-qdbm). Two findings that are
one piece of work.

1. Six hand-rolled walks over `urls.urlpatterns` now exist, and they disagree
   about what counts as a route:
     - test_capabilities.py lines 108, 136, 183: getattr(pattern.callback, "cls", None)
     - test_capabilities.py test_every_route_is_registered_exactly_once: isinstance(pattern, URLPattern)
     - test_telemetry.py:374: isinstance(pattern, URLPattern)
   `.cls` is not where a ViewSet's class lives, so the day any endpoint moves
   behind a router or an include(), three audits stop seeing views and pass
   silently -- and the fix has to be made in six places. helpers.py is the
   documented home for exactly this and says so in its own docstrings
   (`applied`: "Three test modules had a copy of this ... which is what a
   shared helper is for"; `written_by`: "the third copy of the same
   comprehension").

2. The guard added by inventory-tng-qdbm compares route *source text*:
   RoutePattern.__str__ returns the route string and RegexPattern.__str__ the
   regex. So a second registration spelled differently is dead in exactly the
   way api/schema was, and passes. Measured by the reviewer against this
   checkout, all three of these pass both assertions today:
     - path("api/items/<int:id>", ...) beside <int:pk>
     - path("api/labels/<slug:code>", ...) beside <str:code>
     - re_path(r"^api/schema$", ...) beside path("api/schema", ...)

   The property that covers all of them is "every registration is the one that
   answers its own URL":

       assert resolve(reverse(pattern.name, kwargs=arguments)).func == pattern.callback

   and it would have caught the original api/schema duplicate on its own, two
   as_view() calls being two distinct callables. The machinery it needs --
   a specimen per converter so a route with an argument can be reversed at all
   -- already exists at test_telemetry.py:369-381 and would be the second copy
   if written again here.

FIX: put one walk in inventory/tests/helpers.py, yielding the URLPatterns this
repository owns; move the five existing walks onto it; add the reverse/resolve
round-trip once, where every audit gets it. Deferred out of qdbm because it
rewrites four tests that issue did not introduce.
notes:
=== HELD PENDING inventory-tng-81f7.3, added 2026-08-24 ===

This is a REVIEW HOLD, not a real prerequisite, and the distinction matters if you are the one who picks this up when the edge clears.

Nothing in this issue needs anything the demo produces. The dependency is there because the demo builds over the same surface, and this issue's DESCRIPTION may be partly wrong by the time it is unblocked -- built already, superseded, or needing a rewrite to say what is left rather than what was needed. The project owner asked for a mechanism that would not let these be forgotten and would not let them be worked from a stale description.

A dependency was chosen over `bd defer` deliberately. Defer is date-based and needs somebody to guess when; this condition is an EVENT. The edge clears by itself when 81f7.3 closes, which is when the demo has actually been given.

SO THE FIRST THING TO DO WHEN THIS BECOMES READY IS RE-READ IT against what landed, not start work. If the description still holds, carry on. If it does not, revise it before touching code.

THE HOLD ON inventory-tng-81f7.3 IS LIFTED, 2026-08-31, by the same decision the owner made for inventory-tng-2hbv and for the same reason.

It was a REVIEW hold rather than a prerequisite: nothing here needs anything the demo produces, and its purpose was to stop the issue being worked from a description that had gone stale. Re-reading the description against the checkout before starting achieves that, and it was done -- the six walks, their two disagreeing spellings, and the three differently-spelled duplicates were all re-measured rather than taken from the text.
close_reason: One walk in helpers.routes(); all six moved onto it and nothing outside helpers.py mentions urls.urlpatterns. Added the reverse/resolve round-trip, mutation-checked against <int:id> beside <int:pk>, where the counting test passes and this one fails. The walk refuses an unknown converter and an unnamed route rather than skipping, both mutation-checked. One behaviour change held back for 2hbv: the shared walk sees Django's own views as well as DRF's, and each audit now states its own filter rather than inheriting one by accident.

comments.author: Ali Asad Lotia
comments.text:
Line numbers in this issue's description are stale, and there is one more
walk than it counts. Measured on batch/an-open-read-is-argued-too:

  test_capabilities.py .cls walks are at lines 118, 145, 195 and 237, not
  108, 136 and 183. Only 118 and 145 are above the new one at 195.

  They do not share one spelling either: 118 and 237 are plain
  `for pattern in urls.urlpatterns:` + `if view is None: continue`, and 145
  is the generator-inside-a-set-comprehension. The audit inventory-tng-lb95
  added at 195 is a fourth .cls walk and takes the file from 2-1 to 2-2 on
  that split.

Two things the new one does that the others do not, and that the shared walk
should keep when it replaces all of them:

  - it builds the view with the initkwargs the URLconf mounted it with,
    cls(**callback.initkwargs). as_view(permission_classes=[AllowAny]) is
    legal Django and DRF applies it per request, so a bare view() reads a
    route the URLconf deliberately opened as closed. Lines 118, 145 and 237
    and middleware.py:137 all still have that hole; middleware's is the worse
    one, because RequireSecondFactor would refuse a request on a route that
    was opened on purpose.
  - it falls back to view_class when cls is absent, so a non-DRF callback is
    seen rather than skipped. path("admin/login/", RedirectView.as_view(...))
    is in this table today and every other .cls walk is blind to it.

inventory-tng-2hbv is the other half: the walk should be driven through
get_resolver() and ask whether an anonymous request is admitted, rather than
reading urls.urlpatterns and matching class names.

title: urls.py registers api/schema twice
description:
Found by the review of PR #23 (inventory-tng-uq6), pre-existing on main.

backend/src/inventory_tng/urls.py has path('api/schema', SpectacularAPIView.as_view(), name='schema') twice -- once in the middle of the list and once as the last entry. Django resolves the first and reverse() answers the last, so nothing is broken today.

It is worth removing anyway because several tests walk urlpatterns and audit every view they find -- test_capabilities.py does it three times -- so that route is visited twice in each of them, and a future audit that counts rather than sets will be off by one for a reason nobody will look for. Delete the second.
close_reason: Closed

title: The admin offers a Delete on a label the API refuses to delete
description:
Found by the review of PR #22 and its own issue because it predates that change.

LabelAdmin (backend/src/inventory/admin.py:172) is a plain SimpleHistoryAdmin, so the Delete button on a label row is live. Nothing stops it: the label_code_is_printed trigger from migration 0008 is BEFORE UPDATE only, and no model holds a foreign key to Label, so nothing PROTECTs it either.

That contradicts a policy this application states elsewhere. LabelResolveView says of a label: "PATCH of `revoked`, never a delete: the ledger's history refers to what the sticker pointed at", and the API accordingly exposes no DELETE at all. The admin offers one.

inventory-tng-6pr closed the same class of loss one level up -- an item or a location can no longer be deleted under a sticker -- and while doing so it rewrote the guide's blanket "never use it on an item or on a location" into something narrower. The blanket sentence had been covering this case by accident; the narrower one does not.

FIX, to be argued: has_delete_permission returning False on LabelAdmin, so revoking is the only way out and the admin agrees with the API. Or a confirmation that names what the code was on, if there is a real need to remove one -- but nothing in the guides describes such a need, and the code is immutable precisely so that a sticker and a row cannot come apart.

Whichever, it wants a test that the delete is refused, and a line in guides/administrator.md's "About the Delete button".
close_reason: Closed

title: Repository: an ignore file that keeps agents out of generated bulk
description:
Asked for by Ali on 2026-08-24, to reduce what an agent spends context on.

WHAT IS BIG, measured rather than guessed. Tracked files, largest first:

  .beads/issues.jsonl        487 KB   generated by `bd export`
  backend/uv.lock            186 KB   generated by uv
  frontend/package-lock.json 152 KB   generated by npm
  backend/openapi.yaml        73 KB   generated by `manage.py spectacular`
  .beads/interactions.jsonl   66 KB   an append-only audit log

Every one of the five is generated, none is read for meaning, and between them
they are roughly a megabyte an agent can walk into with one `cat` or one broad
grep. Untracked bulk is larger still -- frontend/node_modules is 462 MB,
backend/.venv 197 MB, ignored/ 29 MB, frontend/dist 4.7 MB -- but .gitignore
already keeps most tooling away from those.

WHAT TO WRITE. A top-level `.agentignore` naming the generated files above,
plus the ignored bulk that .gitignore covers for git but not necessarily for a
file-search tool: node_modules/, .venv/, dist/, coverage/, test-results/,
ignored/, .beads/*.jsonl.

TWO THINGS TO SETTLE FIRST, and the second is the one that decides whether
this is worth doing at all:

1. WHICH FILENAME, and whether anything reads it. `.agentignore` is not a
   convention this repository has established and I have not verified that
   Claude Code, Codex or Gemini honour that name -- AGENTS.md is shared by all
   three, so a file only one of them reads is a file the other two walk past.
   Check what each actually supports before choosing; the answer may be
   several files, or a documented convention plus a line in AGENTS.md telling
   an agent to respect it whether or not its harness enforces it.

2. WHETHER IT ADDRESSES THE ACTUAL COST. In the session that prompted this,
   /context attributed 34% of the window to Bash RESULTS -- pytest output,
   checker output, `git` output -- and a negligible share to file reads. An
   ignore file does nothing about that. The measure that would have helped is
   piping command output through head/grep and preferring Read with limits
   over cat. So this is worth doing, and worth doing alongside a line in
   AGENTS.md about command output, or it will be a file that solves the
   smaller half of the problem.

WORTH KNOWING: .beads/issues.jsonl has to stay readable by `bd`, and
check-docs.sh reads `git ls-files`, so whatever is written must not change what
either of those sees. An ignore file for agents is not an ignore file for
tooling.

title: Backend: inventory.refusals cannot say WHICH throttle refused
description:
Raised by the review of PR #21 (finding on api.py:80) and deferred from it, because closing it needs a seam DRF does not offer rather than a fix.

DRF's Throttled carries only its default_code, 'throttled'. So AppendBurstThrottle refusing a volunteer's batch and ReportThrottle refusing the SPA's own client-failure POST both land on inventory.refusals{reason='throttled'} with nothing to tell them apart -- and inventory/throttling.py argues at length that those two must not share a budget ('Losing a report is a cost worth paying; losing the batch is the thing this system exists not to do'). The graph that would show which is happening during an outage shows one line.

WHY IT IS NOT A ONE-LINER. APIView.throttled(request, wait) raises Throttled(wait) and the scope is not on it. check_throttles collects every throttle and raises for the one with the longest wait, so by the time api.exception_handler sees it, which class refused is gone.

OPTIONS:
1. Override throttled() on a shared view base to raise a Throttled subclass carrying the scope. Small, and the scope is a word chosen in this code so cardinality stays bounded -- but it needs a shared base every throttled view actually inherits, and today they do not have one.
2. Attach the scope in AppendThrottle.allow_request when it refuses, on the request, and read it in the handler. Cheaper, uglier: state on the request object read three layers away.
3. Leave it, and say in the counter's declaration that a throttle is counted without saying which. Honest, and costs the distinction.

The same flattening applies on the 403 side and is worth deciding together: SessionAuthentication.enforce_csrf raises a bare PermissionDenied, so a wave of CSRF failures is indistinguishable from volunteers hitting an administrative endpoint -- both are reason='forbidden'.

WHICHEVER IS CHOSEN, a new attribute needs a matching entry in inventory_tng/redaction.py's allowlist.

title: Frontend: the browser's hour and the backend's are not the same hour
description:
Raised by the review of PR #21 (finding on start.ts:80) and deferred from it, because closing it needs a decision about how a deadline reaches the browser rather than a fix.

THE SKEW. debugging.DEFAULT_LIFETIME_SECONDS is 3600 and the signature's clock starts when the token is MINTED. flag.LIFETIME is 3600ms*1000 from when the link is OPENED. So the backend stops honouring the token by however long the link sat in a chat channel before the volunteer tapped it -- minted 10:00, opened 10:50, backend dies 11:00, the browser's timer fires 11:50.

WHAT IT COSTS in that window: nginx's auth_request refuses every span post, the SDK goes on batching and retrying into 403s on a volunteer's data plan, and the badge says 'Recording this device for support' about recording that is no longer happening. sdk.begin() built the exporter with wiring(token), so it holds the token captured at construction and cannot notice.

Bounded by the life of the page, and by the client-side hour that PR #21 does now arm -- so this is a waste and a lie on screen rather than an unbounded leak.

WHY IT IS NOT JUST A FIX. The browser cannot know the mint time. The options each cost something:

1. The link carries the deadline (?trace=<token>&until=<unix>). Cheapest. A forged 'until' cannot extend backend tracing -- the signature is still enforced there -- so the only abuse is keeping a badge up in front of an SDK posting into 403s, which is what already happens. But it puts a second thing in a URL that decision 0021 wants short-lived.
2. /api/debug-trace answers with the remaining seconds and the SPA asks once at settle(). Truthful, costs one request per page load that holds a token, and nginx's auth_request ignores bodies so the ingest path is unaffected.
3. Decode Django's TimestampSigner format in TypeScript. Cheapest to write and the worst: it couples the browser to a Django internal.

RECOMMENDATION: 2, and it wants a line in decision 0021 because it changes what that endpoint is for -- it stops being purely nginx's and becomes something the client asks too.

title: Backend: a command reports through a base class rather than a copied block
description:
Found by /simplify on PR #20, deferred: it is a mechanism change across every command in the tree, which is not what to land in a review cycle's last commit.

Eight commands now open 'with _telemetry.running("<literal>") as counted:', hard-code their own name as a string that duplicates the module filename, call counted.update(_telemetry.figures(...)), and restructure handle so that printing happens outside the block. That restructuring cost real surgery per command: import_sheet grew a _imported staticmethod that exists only to make the run one expression, and profile_sheet was rewritten to build a 'profiled' list. A ninth command needs all of it written again.

PROPOSED: a _telemetry.ReportingCommand(BaseCommand) that overrides handle as a template. Subclasses implement run(**options) -> list[Section]; the base wraps it in running(), derives the command name from self.__module__.rsplit('.', 1)[-1] so there is no literal to drift, records figures(*sections), and prints them after. Every command then loses its with-block, its literal, and its compute-here-print-there split.

seed_integration_data opts out by not inheriting, which is a clearer statement of that exception than the comment plus allowlist entry it carries today.
notes:
CONFIRMED against main at cb5fcb1, 2026-08-24, with one correction to the proposal: the template as described fits six of the eight, not all eight.

VERIFIED:
- Eight commands call _telemetry.running: import_sheet, import_volunteers, stage_sheet, seed_demo_data, mint_debug_token, post_ledger, mint_items, profile_sheet. Every literal duplicates its own module filename exactly.
- seed_integration_data does NOT call it and is the documented exception; it names _telemetry.running only in the comment saying why it does not.
- The surgery is real and admitted in the code. import_sheet._imported is a staticmethod whose own docstring reads 'Split out so the run is one expression the record above can wrap.' profile_sheet builds 'profiled' inside the with and reads it outside.
- Four of them -- stage_sheet, mint_items, post_ledger, import_volunteers -- are byte-for-byte the same five lines apart from the step and the name.

THE CORRECTION. Two do not produce a list of sections, so 'run(**options) -> list[Section]' would not take them:

- mint_debug_token has NO section. It wraps one debugging.mint() call and then writes a token and three lines of prose. It also passes no 'as counted', so it is already a different shape from the other seven.
- seed_demo_data has a section AND prose after it -- a conditional sentence about the ledger, and the label codes to scan. A base that prints the sections and returns cannot emit those.

So the template wants a seam for 'and then say this too', or those two stay as they are and the base serves the six. Six of eight is still worth it; deciding which is part of the work rather than something to settle here.

WORTH KNOWING while doing it: the name is not the only literal. inventory-tng-nb8.11's scripts/check-telemetry.py reads these files, and a base class moving the running() call out of each command changes what that checker sees -- CHANGES maps 'handle' to a path, and a subclass that implements run() rather than handle() would no longer be read as speaking. The checker and this change have to land together, or the allowlist grows eight entries.
close_reason: Six of the eight report through ReportingCommand; the two that produce no section, or say more than one, keep running() directly and the base says which and why.

title: Backend: count every refusal from the one place they all pass through
description:
Found by /simplify on PR #20, deferred because it changes what a collector receives rather than only how the code reads.

inventory.refusals is currently incremented at three sites with three implementations of one idea: inventory/api.py (stale_session, off RecentlyAuthenticated.code), inventory/middleware.py (no_second_factor) and inventory/views.py (unsigned_ingest). A fourth permission class means another isinstance/code comparison in the handler.

Meanwhile Throttled -- handled four lines above in the same function -- is a refusal on account of the caller, which is exactly what the counter's description says, and is counted nowhere.

PROPOSED: api.exception_handler is already the one point every DRF refusal passes through. Count PermissionDenied | NotAuthenticated | Throttled there, with 'reason' read off exc.detail.code -- a closed set of words chosen in this code and in DRF, so cardinality stays bounded -- and let _needs_a_second_look shrink to the body-shaping decision it also makes. A new permission class then gets its counter by declaring a code, which it already has to do.
notes:
CONFIRMED against main at cb5fcb1, 2026-08-24 -- but the PROPOSAL DOES NOT HOLD as written, and that is the important part.

WHAT IS TRUE:
- Three sites, exactly as described: api.py:74 (stale_session), middleware.py:93 (no_second_factor), views.py:1437 (unsigned_ingest).
- Throttled IS handled four lines above the api.py one, in the same function, and is counted nowhere. That half of the finding stands and is worth doing on its own.

WHAT IS FALSE. The proposal says api.exception_handler 'is already the one point every DRF refusal passes through', so counting there would subsume the other two. It would not, because NEITHER OF THE OTHER TWO IS A DRF EXCEPTION:

- middleware.RequireSecondFactor is Django middleware. It does not raise; it RETURNS a redirect or a JsonResponse(status=403) and never enters DRF at all, so no exception handler of DRF's can see it.
- views.py:1437 is DebugTraceVerifyView.get RETURNING Response(status=403). It does not raise either.

So there are not three implementations of one idea. There is one DRF path -- which should count Throttled as well as the two it counts today -- and two deliberate non-raising refusals that will still need their own line wherever they are. Consolidating is a smaller prize than the finding claims.

WHAT IS STILL WORTH DOING, narrowed:
1. Count Throttled in the handler. It is a refusal on account of the caller, which is the counter's own description, and it is free -- the isinstance branch already exists. Give it reason='throttled'.
2. Read 'reason' off exc.detail.code for the PermissionDenied | NotAuthenticated branch rather than off _needs_a_second_look, so a fourth permission class gets its counter by declaring a code. Verify the cardinality claim first: DRF sets a code on every exception it raises, but a view raising PermissionDenied('...') with no code gets the default 'permission_denied', and a caller cannot influence either -- worth confirming that before trusting the set is closed.
3. Leave the middleware and the debug-ingest sites alone, and say in the counter's declaration that not every refusal is a DRF one, so the next reader does not go looking for the consolidation that is not there.

Item 1 alone is a few lines and closes the real gap.
close_reason: Throttled is counted, and the reason is read off the exception rather than named in the handler.

title: One rate per logger, rather than a bespoke variable for one family
description:
Found in the simplify pass over pull request 19, as an altitude finding against inventory-tng-nb8.13.

DJANGO_SECURITY_LOG_RATE is a variable for one logger family. DJANGO_LOG_LEVELS already established the general logger=value shape for the same axis of the same subsystem, and logs.per_logger_levels already parses it. refusals.Bounded is already ninety percent general: it takes the family as a constructor argument and keys its windows by logger name. What is special-cased is the configuration rather than the mechanism.

The module's argument -- that rationing an application logger would hide failures somebody wrote on purpose -- is an argument about the DEFAULT, not about the mechanism, and is equally served by shipping django.security=10/min as the default of DJANGO_LOG_RATES.

SECOND HALF, and the tell is in .env.sample. The filter welds two unrelated policies together: stripping exc_info/exc_text/stack_info, and rationing. .env.sample has to say 'the traceback is dropped from these records whatever this is set to', which is one knob with two behaviours, neither reachable without the other. Quietening a noisy family and de-tracebacking one are separate decisions and want separate filters.

title: Carry the debug flag in OpenTelemetry's context rather than beside it
description:
Found in the simplify pass over pull request 19, as an altitude finding against inventory-tng-nb8.4.

The decision to settle the flag BEFORE Django is right and is the deep part of that change -- the instrumentation's middleware is at the front of the chain, so anything registered as a middleware runs after the span has been created and sampled. The WSGI and ASGI placement follows from it correctly.

The question is only which context carries the answer. Today it is a bespoke ContextVar in inventory_tng/debugging.py, and telemetry.sampler's Debuggable is handed parent_context and ignores it in favour of a module-level lookup. The SDK passes a Context into should_sample precisely so a sampler can be a function of its arguments.

opentelemetry.context.attach/detach with a module key, read via get_value(key, parent_context), would make the flag ride the mechanism that already exists, make the sampler testable without a global, and make it propagate anywhere the SDK's context does. The API package is already a dependency and is cheap to import.

Smaller, same file: guarded and guarded_asgi write the set/try/finally/reset dance twice, and 'reset in finally' is the subtle part.

title: Let gunicorn's access line be fields rather than a format string
description:
Found in the simplify pass over pull request 19, as an altitude finding against inventory-tng-iqff.2.

iqff.2 redacts gunicorn's access line by choosing the format string -- backend/src/inventory_tng/redaction.py holds ACCESS_LOG_FORMAT and ACCESS_LOG_FORMAT_RECORDING, and gunicorn.conf.py sets access_log_format from them. It works and it is verified. What it is not is the same mechanism as everything else: redaction.py's headline claim is 'one answer to is this field allowed, not one per signal to keep in step', and this is a fourth mechanism the claim does not reach. Adding client.address to PERSONAL_ATTRIBUTES changes nothing about the format string and nothing fails.

THE DEEPER FIX. gunicorn's logger_class is a documented extension point. A Logger subclass whose access() emits the atoms it already has as structlog key/values, instead of formatting them into a message, puts the access line inside the same processor chain as every other record -- where redact_record and the one list govern it.

TWO THINGS IT BUYS BEYOND TIDINESS. docs/observability.md currently spends a paragraph on 'one message in this system is assembled rather than written', which would go. And the access record would carry method, status and duration as FIELDS, which is the argument this whole epic makes everywhere else about why structured beats formatted -- today a collector has to regex them back out.

title: Redaction's third mechanism reads a global where the other two take an argument
description: Found in the simplify pass over pull request 19.

title: Ship logs over OTLP with the SDK rather than a hand-rolled encoder
description: backend/src/inventory_tng/shipping.py hand-rolls about 120 lines of OTLP: SEVERITY, the tagged-union value encoder, log_record, the resourceLogs envelope in payload, and a urllib POST -- inside a process that already depends on opentelemetry-sdk and opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http, both pinned at 1.44. Verified: opentelemetry.sdk._logs.LogRecord, Resource/OTELResourceDetector and the HTTP log exporter all import in the backend venv.

title: applied() is written three times in the test suite, and the third copy has diverged
description:
Found in the simplify pass over pull request 19.

backend/src/inventory/tests/test_logging.py defines a context manager that applies a dictConfig with its one handler pointed at a buffer and restores settings.LOGGING afterwards. test_refusals.py copies it and argues for the copy in its own docstring -- 'not imported from it: a test module importing another test module's fixtures makes the second one impossible to read on its own, and this is six lines'. test_redaction.py then copies it again AND diverges, adding redaction.settle() on entry and exit.

So the six-lines argument has already failed inside the batch that made it: there are now two behaviours behind one name in three files, and the divergent one is the one that matters, because it is what stops the personal-data flag leaking between tests.

backend/src/inventory/tests/helpers.py is where this belongs and says why in its own docstring: 'here rather than in conftest.py because they are plain functions ... a helper that is imported reads better at the call site than one that is injected'. One applied(config, admitting=False) there, imported by the three.

It is a new issue rather than a fixup because it spans two of this batch's issues and a file neither of them touched.
acceptance_criteria: One definition, in helpers.py, used by all three modules. The redaction flag is restored whichever module applied a configuration.
close_reason: One applied() in helpers.py, with the redaction reset the third copy had grown, used by all three modules.

title: console.py draws a 'stack' key nothing writes, so a captured stack is never shown
description:
Found reviewing pull request 19, and it predates that branch -- it came in with inventory-tng-nb8.1.

backend/src/inventory_tng/console.py iterates ('stack', 'exception') when drawing the block under a record. 'exception' is right: structlog's format_exc_info writes it. 'stack' is not a key anything writes. structlog's ProcessorFormatter puts record.stack_info into the event dict under 'stack_info', and StackInfoRenderer is deliberately absent from the chain (logs.FROM_LIBRARIES says why), so nothing has ever produced a 'stack' key.

The consequence is small but exact: a developer who writes log.error('...', stack_info=True) sees the stack in JSON and not in the console drawing, and 'pretty-logs' redrawing a saved stream has the same hole. console.STRUCTURAL also names 'stack', so the key is not drawn as key=value either -- which is right for 'stack_info' and is being done under the wrong name.

Fix is to draw 'stack_info' and to name it in STRUCTURAL, and to keep 'stack' only if some stream from elsewhere is expected to carry it -- which is a question about what pretty-logs promises to accept, so decide rather than assume.

inventory-tng-nb8.5 put 'stack_info' on the telemetry allowlist so the key at least reaches a collector; this is the drawing half.
acceptance_criteria: A record carrying stack_info is drawn with its stack in the console, and by scripts/pretty-logs over a saved stream. A test holds both.
close_reason: Closed

title: Both: make logging and instrumentation something the build checks
description:
Ali's requirement that all work after the retroactive sweep is extensively logged and instrumentable. A Definition of Done line alone will not hold, for the same reason the documentation rules needed check-docs.py.

BEING HONEST ABOUT WHAT A CHECKER CAN PROVE. Auto-instrumentation makes a span for every route and every query for free, so asserting that an endpoint has a span proves nothing about whether anybody instrumented anything. The deliberate part is what needs enforcing.

PROPOSED, in the shape of scripts/check-docs.py: every module defining a DRF view, a management command or a sheet step has a module logger and at least one domain record on its state-changing paths, with a check-telemetry.allow file for the justified exceptions -- the same escape hatch check-docs.allow already has, so an exception is a visible decision rather than a silent gap. Plus a test walking the URLconf asserting every route produces a span with a real name rather than a fallback.

DEVELOPERS.md#definition-of-done gains the line, and it must not be a second copy of what the checker enforces.

Last of the epic on purpose: a checker written before the retroactive sweep would fail on every file it was meant to protect.
acceptance_criteria: A new view with no logging fails the build. The allowlist is small and each entry says why. The Definition of Done links rather than restates.
notes:
LANDED. What was actually done, and where the paused note above was wrong.

THE FIVE FAILING CASES WERE THE HARNESS, not the checker. The suite called
'check run_check' with no arguments, so testlib's expect passed the reader no
file at all: it read nothing, printed nothing and exited 0. Every case wanting
a complaint failed, and the two allowlist cases reported a stale allowance
because nothing had been read for it to excuse. The checker's own logic --
has_a_logger's ImportFrom arm, and the ordering of the read set against the
allowance -- was already right and was not touched.

THE SUITE NOW DRIVES THE REAL ENTRY POINT, in the shape of check-docs.test.sh:
a throwaway git repo per case with report.sh, the reader and check-telemetry.sh
copied into its scripts/, the module written under backend/src/inventory/ and
staged. That covers the half the old shape could not -- the corpus, the
exclusion of tests/, the allowlist's address -- and gained two cases: a test
module that changes something is not asked to say so, and a file that will not
parse exits 2 saying nothing was checked rather than printing the all-clear.
12 cases, and mutating either the corpus glob or the allowlist check fails 6
and 3 of them respectively.

THE URLCONF TEST is test_and_so_is_every_other_route_in_the_urlconf in
backend/src/inventory/tests/test_telemetry.py. It walks urls.urlpatterns,
skips includes, builds a specimen argument per route converter so a
parameterised route can be asked for at all, and asserts each request's SERVER
span carries http.route equal to the pattern the URLconf holds, is not named
for its method alone, and does not carry the value it was asked with.

CI: 'Check the telemetry checker' in the Guardrail checkers job, 'Check for
silent changes' in the Documentation job.

DOCS: a Definition of Done line linking to the checker and to
docs/observability.md, and a paragraph in docs/observability.md saying the rule
is enforced. mint_debug_token gained a test that it says it handed a token out.
close_reason: The checker, its suite, the URLconf test, CI and the Definition of Done line all landed.

title: 'git push --force' is on the ask-first row and nothing enforces it
description:
AGENTS.md singles out a bare 'git push --force' as needing approval every time, and explains why: --force-with-lease refuses if anything arrived since you last fetched, and a bare --force has no such guard.

Nothing implements that. .claude/settings.local.json allows Bash(git *), which covers it, and the landing gate's push-main arm only fires on a push aimed at main -- a bare --force to a batch branch matches neither. An agent that trusts the row will run it after somebody else has pushed, and their commits are gone: precisely the loss the row exists to prevent.

Found by the /code-review pass on PR #15, which observed that the ask-first row was re-published without its remaining items being audited.
acceptance_criteria: Either a bare --force is refused by the same mechanism that guards the other ask-first items, or AGENTS.md stops implying it is guarded.
close_reason: The gate refuses a bare --force and its short form -f, and permits --force-with-lease, so the ask-first row is enforced by the same mechanism as the other items on it rather than only written down. AGENTS.md links to what the gate refuses instead of restating it.

title: DESIGN: append ingress.host to ALLOWED_HOSTS instead of guarding it at render time
description:
inventory-tng-adj established the pattern that a host only the deployment knows gets appended rather than required to be listed: DJANGO_POD_IP comes in through the downward API and joins ALLOWED_HOSTS.

The /simplify altitude pass on PR #14 argued ingress.host is exactly such a host, and that appending it would be strictly better than the inventory-tng.ingressHostIsAllowed guard adj shipped:

- the guard restates Django's is_same_domain matching in Go templates, so there are two copies of one rule (PR #14 shipped it stricter than Django on its first day -- no apex arm, no lowercasing -- and the fix was to pin it to Django with a test rather than to remove the copy)
- appending makes the misconfiguration unrepresentable rather than refused
- django.allowedHosts demotes to 'other names a browser may use', which is a knob with less to get wrong
- test_chart.py stops having to pass ingress.enabled=false to get probe cases past a guard that has nothing to do with probes

Not taken on PR #14 because the guard also fails loudly at install time, which is worth something on a chart nobody has yet installed, and because it would reopen a design the pull request had already reviewed and agreed.

The counter-argument to weigh: appending widens what Django answers to without an operator writing it down. Against that, the ingress host is by definition a name browsers use, and the ingress routes it to this pod already.
design: Decide between: (a) keep the guard, as today; (b) append ingress.host in backendEnv when ingress.enabled, delete the guard and its two tests; (c) both -- append, and keep a guard that only warns.
acceptance_criteria: A decision is recorded, in docs/decisions/ if it changes the chart's contract.

title: urls.py registers api/schema twice
description:
Found while fixing the review of PR #13 on 2026-08-22, in code that batch does not touch.

backend/src/inventory_tng/urls.py has path('api/schema', ...) at two places, from commit 9e2e86a. Django resolves the first and the second is dead. Harmless today, and exactly the sort of thing that becomes confusing when somebody changes one of them and cannot see why nothing happened.

FIX: delete the later registration, and add whatever assertion would have caught it -- test_api_schema.py already enumerates the operations and is the natural home.
notes:
DUPLICATE of inventory-tng-qdbm, which fixed this in PR #25 (2026-08-24): the
later api/schema registration is deleted, and
test_capabilities.py::test_every_route_is_registered_exactly_once guards the
general property -- no route and no reverse() name registered twice -- so the
next duplicate fails a test. Do not work this issue; there is nothing left of
it.

Left open only because check-commit.sh permits one issue to move to closed per
commit and qdbm's commit is that one. Close it with the next landing.

The FIX line above suggested test_api_schema.py as the home. It went to
test_capabilities.py instead, which already held three walks over urlpatterns
for the guard to sit beside.
close_reason: Duplicate of inventory-tng-qdbm, landed as 4c1e521. Held out of that commit only because check-commit.sh permits one issue to move to closed per commit; this closure rides out with the next landing.

title: Say how an outside contributor gets their work in
description:
Found by a new contributor following the documents on 2026-08-22.

CONTRIBUTING.md says to fork the repository and create a branch. DEVELOPERS.md's Pull requests section assumes you push batch/* to this repository and that main is protected here. Somebody without push access is told two incompatible things, and the whole review cycle -- one batch one branch, the landing gate, the batch-contents comment -- is written for a maintainer.

NYC Mesh is a volunteer project, so the outside contributor is the normal case rather than the exception.

FIX: one short section saying which half of the cycle applies to a fork and which does not, in whichever of the two documents owns it -- and only in that one.

title: backend.port and frontend.port are knobs neither image honours
description:
Found by a deployment review on 2026-08-22.

infra/helm/inventory-tng/values.yaml exposes backend.port and frontend.port, but backend/Dockerfile hardcodes gunicorn --bind 0.0.0.0:8000 and frontend/nginx.conf.template hardcodes listen 8080. Changing either value renders a consistent-looking Deployment, Service and Ingress that route to a port nothing is listening on, and the failure is a connection refused with no clue where it came from.

FIX: either make the images read the port from the environment, or remove the values so the chart stops offering a setting it cannot keep.

title: Point the compose healthcheck at a database that exists
description:
compose.yaml's postgres healthcheck runs 'pg_isready -U $POSTGRES_USER' with no -d, so it connects to a database named after the user -- 'inventory' -- which the stack never creates. pg_isready still reports the server as accepting connections, so the healthcheck passes, but every probe leaves 'FATAL: database "inventory" does not exist' in the postgres log, five seconds apart, for as long as the stack is up.

Noticed while testing the hardening in inventory-tng-61c. The fix is to add -d with the same POSTGRES_DB the service is given.
close_reason: pg_isready names POSTGRES_DB as well as POSTGRES_USER, so the probe asks for the database the stack creates.

title: Group a multi-issue batch under an epic
description:
DEVELOPERS.md#pull-requests requires a batch of more than one issue to be grouped under an epic 'so that what belongs to it is recorded rather than remembered'. Pull request 7 landed four issues -- 2zx, kx6, a7j and hr2 -- with no epic and no parent edges, while every earlier multi-issue batch has one (c6j, c6b, 2lo, 8fp, z6t).

scripts/check-batch.sh passes because with no epic there is no membership to check, which is the wrong way round: the absence of the grouping is exactly what should fail. Either the checker gains that check or the rule is relaxed deliberately, but the current state means a batch can skip it silently.
acceptance_criteria: A multi-issue batch without an epic is either impossible or reported, and the decision between those two is recorded.
close_reason: batch-membership.py refuses a multi-issue range with no epic, with a test case; the rule is enforced rather than remembered.

title: Say every over-long body line, not just the first
description:
check-commit.sh breaks out of the body-width loop after the first line over 72 columns, so a message with three long lines takes three runs to fix. Every other rule it checks reports in full.

Noticed while landing inventory-tng-spk: three round trips for one message, and the third only because the second fix was written by hand against a report that named one line.
close_reason: Every over-long body line is reported in one run, with each shown, rather than the first and a break.

title: An epic's closure counts as work it never did
description:
check-commit.sh refuses a commit whose staged tracker moves two issues to closed. That is right for work, and wrong for an epic: an epic groups a batch and carries no work of its own, so closing it alongside the last bead of its batch is bookkeeping, not a second unit.

Today the only ways out are to leave the epic open after its batch merges, or to give its closure a commit of its own -- which then has a Closes trailer for something nobody implemented.

Ignore issues of type epic when counting closures, and say so in DEVELOPERS.md Commits. bd epic close-eligible already knows when one is finished.

Noticed while landing inventory-tng-b8n, when the batch-1 epic's close collided with it.
close_reason: An epic is not counted as a closure: it groups a batch and does no work of its own.

title: The read boundary is a glob, not the principle
description:
DEVELOPERS.md states the line well: a script header documents the repository and is where a guide's explanation gets re-derived, while a docstring beside the invariant it enforces is code explaining itself. check-docs.sh implements that as scripts/*.sh and scripts/*.py, which is a location rather than the distinction.

By the stated test, batch-membership.py and ci-check-names.py are helpers whose docstrings are code explaining itself, and they are read; .github/workflows/ci.yml, whose comments repo-settings.sh's whole design depends on, is not. Move a helper out of scripts/ and it stops being checked, with no signal.

Raised by the simplify pass on pull request 2. Related to inventory-tng-lwe.
close_reason: The boundary is an exclusion of application source, so a file added or moved is read by default; workflows and the chart are read now.

title: Make the message rules a module, not a subprocess to scrape
description:
check-batch.sh delegates the message rules to check-commit.sh by forking it once per commit and grepping the failure glyph out of its stdout, then re-wrapping each scraped line with the commit's short sha. Two scripts that sit beside each other and already source a shared library are talking over stdout text, and the re-wrap flattens any objection that runs to two lines.

Delegating is right -- the rules must have one home, and a subprocess guarantees a contributor's hook and CI enforce identical text. The mechanism is what is a layer too low. A sourced module holding the rules as functions, with check-commit.sh as the command-line interface over it, removes the scraping and the fork per commit.

Raised by the simplify pass on pull request 2.
close_reason: The message rules are scripts/message-rules.sh, sourced by both checkers; check-batch.sh calls them instead of forking check-commit.sh and grepping its stdout.

title: The new receipt file is not ignored
description:
.gitignore lists .claude/.landing-receipt.json, which the landing gate stopped writing when inventory-tng-c6j.8 reworked it to key receipts on the pull request. It now writes .claude/.review-receipts.json, which nothing ignores, so it shows up as untracked in every git status and is one 'git add -A' away from being committed.

Local machinery, like the hook that writes it, and should be ignored the same way.
close_reason: One pattern matches whatever the local gate calls its receipt, rather than listing a name that has already changed once.

title: Read application code comments for duplicated prose too
description:
check-docs.sh reads Markdown and the headers of scripts/. Pointing it at backend/ and frontend/ as well finds 64 more passages living in two places, most of them a model or view docstring reproducing docs/data-model.md or a decision record, and tests restating the module they test.

They are real by the letter of the rule, but they are a different genre from a topic having two homes: a docstring beside the invariant it enforces is the code explaining itself. Each needs deciding on its own -- some should be deleted and linked, some are the right kind of repetition and want an allowance naming the pair.

Sixty-four judgements is a batch, not a step in the issue that widened the input set. Raised while doing inventory-tng-5yf.
acceptance_criteria: check-docs.sh reads backend/ and frontend/ comments, and the repository passes with an allowlist whose every entry is justified.
close_reason: Closed

title: Name the CI jobs for what they now do
description:
The commit-check job is still called 'Commit checker' while running four checker suites, and the docs job is still 'Documentation links' while also running the duplication check. Both names describe what the job was when it had one step.

Renaming used to be dangerous: the required-check names were hardcoded in repo-settings.sh, so a rename silently un-required the job on main. They are now read out of ci.yml, so a rename is safe as long as repo-settings.sh is rerun -- which is the point of deriving them.
close_reason: Commit checker is Guardrail checkers; Documentation links is Documentation. Safe because the required-check names are read out of ci.yml.

title: Stop hand-maintaining the batch list in the template
description:
The pull request template asks for a table of the issues in the batch and a checkbox asserting every commit holds exactly one issue. Both are facts the machinery already owns: the epic records membership, batch-membership.py verifies it against the branch, and the required 'One issue per commit' check decides the proposition the checkbox asserts.

Pull request 1 proved the cost -- inventory-tng-724 joined the batch late and the table went stale with nothing to notice. A ticked box asserting a machine-checked fact also trains people to tick boxes.

Drop both. If the membership belongs in the pull request, have the history job post what check-batch.sh already knows, so the list is verified rather than typed.
close_reason: The template stops asking for the batch list and the machine-checked checkbox; the history job posts what check-batch.sh --list read off the commits.

title: The tracker diff is read twice on every commit
description:
check-commit.sh runs git diff --cached over .beads/issues.jsonl twice: once to find what closed, once with --name-only to ask whether the path was staged at all. The first diff already answers the second question by being empty or not.

This runs as a commit-msg hook on every local commit against a 180KB tracker. Predates the pull-request-workflow batch, so it was not fixed there.

Raised by the simplify pass on pull request 1.
close_reason: One git diff, used for both questions: what closed, and whether the tracker was staged at all.

title: Nothing runs the settings check
description:
repo-settings.sh exists because settings left as something somebody once clicked drift unnoticed. The remedy shipped is a script run by hand plus a sentence telling you to remember to run it, so the failure mode survives one level up: protection can be relaxed in the web UI and main will accept things it should not, with no signal.

enforce_admins, allow_force_pushes and required_linear_history are exactly the settings that cannot be enforced from the repository, so their silent loss is the most expensive drift available. A weekly scheduled workflow running --check would catch it; it needs a token with Administration: read.

Raised by the simplify pass on pull request 1.
close_reason: A weekly scheduled job runs repo-settings.sh --check, and any pull request touching CI's job names runs it too.

title: An allowance should name the pair it was granted for
description:
check-docs.sh's is_allowed tests containment against every allowed passage regardless of which files collided. Once README.md and 0008 are allowed, the same passage appearing in a fourth file is permitted too, silently and forever.

Make an entry name its two files plus the passage. A third copy then fails, and an allowance that matched nothing can be reported as dead -- which makes the baseline self-deleting rather than permanent.

Raised by the simplify pass on pull request 1.
close_reason: An allowance names the two files it covers; a third copy is refused, and an allowance matching nothing is reported so the baseline cannot outlive its debt.

title: Two passages live in two files
description:
check-docs.sh found two explanations pasted into a second file, both predating it, so they are baselined in scripts/check-docs.allow rather than fixed under the issue that added the checker:

- README.md and docs/decisions/0008 on why a correction cannot be expressed
- docs/briefs/authorisation.md and docs/decisions/0014 on signing in not navigating

For each, decide which file owns it, delete the other copy, link instead, and remove its line from the allowlist. A brief is the investigation and the decision is the conclusion, so the decision most likely owns it.
close_reason: README defers to 0008 for the correction evidence; the authorisation brief defers to 0014 for what one interface means. The allowlist is empty.

title: A scanner that has stopped reading looks exactly like a shelf with no labels on it
description:
frontend/src/scan/decodeLoop.ts reads a rejected decode as 'no code in this frame', which is right for the ordinary case -- most frames are a shelf, or a label mid-focus -- and wrong for the permanent one. A detector whose every call throws (an unbound method, a detached ArrayBuffer, a WASM heap that will not grow, a tainted canvas) is indistinguishable from a volunteer pointing the phone at nothing: the preview is live and moving, the loop keeps ticking five times a second, and there is no message, no console output and no counter anywhere that says the scanner is dead.

The same gap has a second half. `frame()` and `onCode()` are deliberately left OUTSIDE the swallow, on the argument that a bug there should surface rather than hide -- but nothing surfaces it either. The interval callback is async and its promise is unhandled, so what actually happens is an unhandled rejection five times a second for as long as the camera is open, which no error boundary sees and no volunteer is told about.

WHAT TO DECIDE

This is a product decision before it is a code one, which is why it is not a review fix:

- How many consecutive failures mean 'stopped' rather than 'unlucky'? At 5 Hz even a second of failures is five.
- What does the volunteer see? Something like 'the scanner has stopped reading -- close and reopen the camera, or type the code printed under the QR' names a way out, which is the standard the rest of scan/ holds itself to (see NO_CAMERA and refusal() in CameraScanner.tsx).
- Does the loop stop itself at that point, or keep trying? Keeping the lens powered for a loop that cannot decode costs battery for nothing.

Whatever is decided, the failure has to leave the loop by a route the component can see -- an onFailure alongside onCode is the obvious shape -- rather than being counted inside a module that has no screen.

Raised by the xhigh review of inventory-tng-w1e, which found both halves and correctly declined to invent the policy.
acceptance_criteria: A detector that fails repeatedly stops being read as an empty shelf: the volunteer is told the scanner has stopped reading and what to do instead, and a frame source or onCode that throws no longer escapes as an unhandled rejection. Both paths tested in decodeLoop.test.ts.
close_reason: A run of refusals stops the loop and tells the volunteer; a frame source or onCode that throws does the same instead of becoming an unhandled rejection.

title: CameraScanner is 68% covered, and most of the gap is testable
description:
CameraScanner.tsx sits at 68% lines while the rest of the frontend is 95-100%, and it is the single reason the project total is 94.8% rather than ~97%. The uncovered block is lines 135-182 and 192: everything from getUserMedia resolving through to the decode loop and its teardown.

It was left that way on the judgement that covering it means faking a camera, which would prove the fakes work rather than the code. That judgement is right about faking the DECODE and wrong about faking the LIFECYCLE, which was not checked at the time. It has now been checked.

WHAT WAS MEASURED

A throwaway test of about twenty lines -- stubbing navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia and enumerateDevices, and spying HTMLMediaElement.prototype.play -- rendered the component, ran open() to completion, and on unmount the fake track's stop() was genuinely called. That single test covered 48.68% of the file on its own. So the stream lifecycle is reachable in jsdom today with no new tooling.

Where it stops is loadDetector(), which dynamically imports the real WebAssembly module; under Node that fails on the wasm URL. Past that point the decode loop is reachable only with vi.mock of ./decoder.

THE THREE BANDS, AND WHICH DESERVE A TEST

1. getUserMedia -> srcObject -> play() -> listCameras -> teardown. Reachable now. A test here asserts our own rules, not a fake's behaviour: that the stream is assigned before play, that every track is stopped on cleanup, and that a stream or a timer arriving AFTER teardown is still released. Two of those were real bugs a review caught, so they have earned tests.

2. The decode loop, with a faked detector. Also our own rules: skip while busy, recheck live after the await, hand every code in a frame to onCode, treat a decode failure as the ordinary case rather than an error. The post-await live recheck was itself a bug found in review -- a decode landing after the volunteer closed the scanner added a line to the batch.

3. That zxing actually reads a QR from a real frame. NOT this bead. No test here may claim it, and a fake detector returning a canned rawValue must not be dressed up as proof of decoding. That is inventory-tng-qsu.

APPROACH

Prefer extracting band 2 over stubbing it in place. The loop's policy is a function of an injected detect, an injected frame source and an injected liveness check; pulled into its own module it is plainly unit-testable, and the component drops to wiring -- the same move that produced frame.ts, cameras.ts, confirm.ts and decoder.ts, and the reason those are all covered while this file is not. Band 1 stays in the component, tested with the stubs above, because it is about the component.

Coverage is the side effect here, not the goal. A pile of stubs in CameraScanner.test.tsx would reach a similar number without the improvement; that is not what this bead asks for.

NOT ACCEPTABLE AS A SOLUTION: a coverage exclusion (the project forbids one), moving the file out of the include glob, or lowering the threshold. Whether the 90% gate should be per-directory rather than global is a fair question but a separate one -- the frontend currently has about 29 lines of headroom, and the next untestable browser API could fail the build for a reason that is not a quality regression.

RELATIONSHIP TO inventory-tng-qsu: if this lands first, that bead gets smaller. Its job narrows to the one assertion only a real browser can make -- that a real frame carrying a real symbol produces a cart line -- because everything around it will already be covered here.

Raised from a question about why frontend coverage sits below the backend's.
acceptance_criteria: The decode loop's policy is tested independently of any real camera or decoder, and the stream lifecycle is tested through the component, including that a stream or timer arriving after teardown is released. No test claims to prove that a QR code decodes. No coverage exclusion is added.
close_reason: The decode loop is now its own module with its own tests, and the stream lifecycle is tested through the component. CameraScanner.tsx went 68% -> 100%, the frontend 94.8% -> 98.9% lines, with no coverage exclusion. Two things the work found: the post-loop 'if (!live) release()' was unreachable (nothing awaits between it and the check above), and a stream granted before a later failure was never released at all -- both fixed. inventory-tng-spk was raised for the decoder's poisoned promise, which is decoder.ts's own bug.

title: Leftovers from the batch-3 simplify pass
description:
Small items found by the reuse and simplification reviews of inventory-tng-p3t, ea6 and vci, judged real but left for later so the batch could land. None changes behaviour.

1. frontend/src/scan/: the label fixtures (PACKET, WALL, a cable label) and the "two reads a code costs" fetch stub are copy-pasted into DeepLink.test.tsx, Scanner.test.tsx and applyCode.test.ts. scan/testFixtures.ts already exists for this directory and holds only the camera fixtures. A field added to ResolvedLabel is four edits.

2. frontend/src/batch/movements.ts: movementFor() calls sideFor(cart.kind) inside the map and re-checks cart.locationId per line, though both are constant for the batch. Compute once in batchBody and pass it.

3. frontend/src/storage.ts: isText is typed as returning boolean rather than as a "value is string" type predicate, which is the only reason cameras.ts declares its own inline predicate. Widening it satisfies the Shape type unchanged.

4. frontend/src/scan/outcome.tsx exports announcement(), which nothing outside the file imports.

5. frontend/src/scan/Scanner.tsx has a .catch on the applyCode promise that is unreachable as written -- no signal is passed and applyCode answers rather than throws -- so it now only swallows genuine bugs.

Each is a few lines. Worth doing together rather than one at a time.
acceptance_criteria: All five are addressed or each one that is not has a reason recorded here.
notes:
Item 5 was NOT done, and the reason is that the bead's premise was wrong. The .catch on the applyCode promise is reachable: DeepLink passes an AbortSignal and aborts it on unmount, so an abandoned deep-link scan lands there. useScannedCode's comment already says so. The other four are done.

Item 1 landed in two halves: the label fixtures (PACKET, WALL, CABLE_LABEL) and the fetch stub (serving, refusing) both live in scan/testFixtures.ts now. A review caught that consolidating the fixtures had given WALL and the cable label the same code, which was invisible while they lived in separate files; WALL now has its own.
close_reason: Closed

title: Nothing verifies the label decoder is served from our own origin
description:
inventory-tng-p3t's acceptance criteria include 'the wasm asset is served from our own origin' -- a non-optional constraint from decision 0011 section 2, because the page has to work in a basement and the frontend image is self-contained.

What exists today: a unit test asserting locateFile() returns a non-http(s) path, and a manual check of the build output. What does not exist is anything that fails when the assertion stops being true. The jsdelivr URL is still present in the ponyfill chunk as zxing-wasm's dead default, so a regression that let it be used would look exactly like today's build to every automated check.

frontend/integration/ is the right home: a Playwright test that opens the camera and asserts every request for a .wasm went to the page's own origin -- and that none went to a CDN. The agent that built the scanner left it out because integration/ was outside its file scope, and said so.

Raised by a review of inventory-tng-p3t.
acceptance_criteria: A test fails if the decoder binary is fetched from anywhere but the origin serving the app.
close_reason: Closed

title: The explanation for a missing camera is unreachable by the person who needs it
description:
frontend/src/scan/Scanner.tsx renders the Camera button only when cameraSupported() is true, and the "camera" state can only become true through that button. CameraScanner.tsx then checks cameraSupported() again and, when false, renders a 40-word message naming the commonest real cause -- that the page was reached over plain HTTP at a LAN address, which is why getUserMedia is not there.

That message can never be seen by a volunteer. They get a silently missing button instead, on exactly the setup where the explanation would tell them what to do. The branch is reached only by CameraScanner.test.tsx.

Two ways out, and they are opposite: drop the guard in CameraScanner so one place decides, or drop Scanner gate so the explanation reaches the person who needs it. The second is what the message was written for.

Raised by a review of inventory-tng-p3t.
acceptance_criteria: A volunteer on a device or origin where the camera cannot work is told why, rather than shown nothing. Only one place decides whether the camera is on offer.
close_reason: Closed

title: Every cart change re-renders every catalogue row
description:
frontend/src/items/ItemRow.tsx is not memoized -- there is no React.memo anywhere in frontend/src -- and CartProvider hands a new context value on every cart change. So one scan re-renders all 50 rows of the page, each rebuilding a Set and sorting it in packetSizes(), running a reduce in onHand(), and doing a linear cart.lines.find().

Measured in jsdom with 50 rows: a keystroke-triggered re-render costs about 30 ms; wrapping the export in React.memo drops it to 2.5-4.6 ms, roughly 7x, because data.results object identities are unchanged until a new response arrives. It does not help the cart-dispatch render, which is a context update and bypasses memo -- that one wants the per-row work hoisted or memoized instead.

Pre-existing rather than introduced by any one bead: it was measured during a review of inventory-tng-p3t, on code from inventory-tng-6su.

Note the related finding already fixed: CartProvider's dispatch is now stable across cart changes, so an effect depending on it no longer re-runs per scan.
acceptance_criteria: A cart change does not rebuild the packaging chips and balances of every row on the page. The measurement that justifies whatever is done is in the test or a comment.
close_reason: Closed

title: The camera decode loop allocates a canvas and two full-frame buffers per tick
description:
frontend/src/scan/CameraScanner.tsx passes the HTMLVideoElement straight to detector.detect(), which takes barcode-detector's slow path: it allocates a NEW OffscreenCanvas and 2D context on every call (never reused), draws the frame, and getImageData's it back from the GPU into a fresh Uint8ClampedArray of width*height*4. zxing-wasm then runs a plain-JS per-pixel loop into another width*height grayscale buffer and memcpys that into the WASM heap.

Measured at 640x480 and the loop's 5 Hz: about 7.7 MB/s of garbage, 1.5 M JS loop iterations per second, and 5 GPU readbacks per second. constraints() in cameras.ts asks for no width/height, so a device that answers 1280x720 makes all of it 4x -- and nothing in the code knows which it got. This is the battery cost DECODE_INTERVAL_MS's comment is trying to bound, and it is unbounded in the dimension that matters.

The fix: keep one canvas in a ref, drawImage scaled to a fixed working size (~640 on the long edge), getImageData from that, and hand the resulting ImageData to detect() -- which then takes the fast path and allocates nothing of its own. That caps the pixel count whatever the camera returns and removes the per-tick canvas. Adding width: { ideal: 1280 } to constraints() would at least make the cost knowable.

Raised by a review of inventory-tng-p3t and measured against the installed barcode-detector/zxing-wasm.
acceptance_criteria: One canvas is reused across ticks and the decoded frame is a bounded size whatever resolution the camera returns. The measured per-tick allocation is stated in a comment so the next reader does not have to re-derive it.
notes:
Done, with one limit worth knowing: per-tick allocation is reduced, not removed. getImageData must return a fresh ImageData each tick, so about 5.8 MB/s at 640x360 remains, against 7.7 MB/s at 640x480 before and roughly three times that from an unconstrained 720p phone. What is gone outright is the per-tick canvas and 2D context, and the growth with whatever resolution the camera chose.

A review noted that constraints() now asks width ideal 1280, which raises as well as lowers: a laptop webcam that would have answered 640x480 is now asked for 720p, so the drawImage that frame.ts cannot avoid got larger on exactly the devices that were already cheap. Kept because the preview and autofocus are worth it, and said so in the docstring rather than left as an accident.
close_reason: Closed

title: LabelSheetView inherits ListAPIView to answer with a document
description:
GET /api/labels/sheet answers with an HTML page, not a list of rows, and four accommodations stack up to make a list view do that:

- list() is overridden not to serialize
- serializer_class is set to a serializer the code itself documents as never rendering anything, because ListAPIView asks for one
- filterset_class declares a 'code' parameter drf-spectacular cannot read for a non-list operation, so the parameter is re-declared by hand in @extend_schema
- LabelSheetRenderer has to know DRF's {'detail': ...} error shape in order to render a refusal as a page

Staying inside DRF is right and should not change: permissions, throttles, the exception handler and open_to_anybody all come free, and the HTML media type is deliberate (a JSON body of SVG strings would put the dimensions that decide whether a label scans on the far side of the API from the tests that assert them).

What is wrong is the base class. An APIView with a get() that reads 'code' off query_params, filters LIVE_LABELS and returns HttpResponse(sheet(...), content_type='text/html') drops all four: DRF's finalize_response passes a non-Response through untouched. The one thing worth keeping is the HTML-rendered 403, which becomes a small handle_exception override rather than a renderer class.

Raised by a review of inventory-tng-n2o. Not urgent -- the endpoint works and is tested -- but the comment in views.py now points here rather than justifying the field.
acceptance_criteria: The sheet endpoint carries no serializer it does not use and no hand-written duplicate of a parameter its filter declares, and the refusal is still an HTML page. Tests unchanged in what they assert.
close_reason: Closed

title: The schema does not describe the 400 a refused write answers with
description:
PolicyAwareAutoSchema (backend/src/inventory/api.py) derives 403, 404 and 429 from the view's own policy, but nothing derives 400. So none of the catalogue write operations publishes a shape for the validation refusals its serializers produce, even though inventory-tng-0rr added validators specifically so a client would get a 400 naming the field rather than a 500 naming nothing.

A client generated from openapi.yaml has no type for the body of POST /api/items with reorder_quantity 0, POST /api/locations with a custody location and no holder, or PATCH /api/categories/{id} with a looping parent.

The contract is also inconsistent with itself: POST /api/stock/transactions documents its 400 explicitly, through BatchRejectedSerializer, because its body is bespoke -- a flat list of errors carrying the index of the offending line.

What needs deciding is the shape to publish for the ordinary case. DRF renders a field map, {field: [messages]}, plus non_field_errors for complaints about the body as a whole. That is not expressible as a Serializer's own fields, so it needs either a hand-written OpenApiResponse with additionalProperties, or a decision to give the catalogue writes the same flat errors array the batch endpoint uses -- which would be one error shape across the whole API and is probably the better answer, at the cost of changing a response clients already read.

Raised by a review of inventory-tng-0rr.
acceptance_criteria: Every operation that can answer 400 describes the body it answers with, and the description is generated rather than repeated per view. A decision records whether the API has one error shape or two.
notes:
Decision: the API keeps two error shapes, and this bead describes both rather than unifying them.

Considered: giving the catalogue writes the flat {detail, errors: [{index, field, detail}]} body the batch endpoint uses, so the whole API had one error shape. Rejected:

1. It changes a response clients already read. The bead is about the schema being silent, not about the body being wrong; DRF renders the field map today and a client written against a running server already handles it. Changing it would be a breaking change made in passing, in a bead whose acceptance criterion is a description.
2. The two shapes are not describing the same thing. A batch is refused line by line and a line is identified by its position in the submitted array; a map keyed by field name has nowhere to put an index, so unifying downward loses information. Unifying upward -- giving every single-row write an index that is always null -- pays that cost on eleven operations to spare one.
3. The field map is what DRF produces unaided. Adopting the flat shape everywhere means an exception handler or a per-view wrapper on every catalogue write, so the API would carry code to make its refusals uniform rather than carry a schema that says what they are.

Implemented instead: PolicyAwareAutoSchema derives 400 the way it already derives 403, 404 and 429 -- from the operation having a request body to refuse -- and publishes a ValidationError component (object, additionalProperties: array of string). setdefault leaves POST /api/stock/transactions its BatchRejected. If one shape is wanted later it is a versioned change of its own, with the frontend in scope.
close_reason: Closed

title: No test renders an admin page, because staticfiles has no manifest under test
description:
Decision 0014 point 4 keeps the Django admin as the fallback that works when the single-page app does not. A test now proves every model is registered, but nothing proves a page actually renders.

An attempt to add one failed with ValueError: Missing staticfiles manifest entry for 'admin/css/base.css'. Whitenoise's manifest storage expects collectstatic to have run, which the test environment does not do. The deployed image does collect static, so this is a test-environment gap rather than an admin defect -- but it means the only existing admin test (in test_models.py) POSTs and asserts a 302, never rendering a template.

So a changelist that raises on render -- a stale list_display naming a removed field, a broken __str__, a bad ModelAdmin method -- would pass every test we have. Django's own checks framework catches some of that (checks.run_checks(tags=['admin']) is now run), but not everything that only appears at render time.

The fix is a test-settings override of STORAGES for staticfiles, which touches settings.py. Found by the agent implementing inventory-tng-cck, which left it alone rather than reach outside its file scope.
acceptance_criteria: A test renders the changelist and change form of every registered model and fails if either raises.
close_reason: Closed

title: Restrict the administrative routes at the network
description:
Decision 0013 point 6. Administrators are few and their locations predictable, unlike volunteers, who are on a phone wherever the stock happens to be. Restricting the administrative routes to the mesh, a VPN or an identity-aware proxy costs those few people very little, and it is the one place a network boundary fits without excluding the person this project exists to serve.

Expressed in the ingress and the network rather than in the application, so its absence is not something the code can detect. That makes it a stated precondition in docs/deployment.md, alongside the existing one about the ingress being the only route to the frontend pod.

Not before the rest of 0012 to 0014: this narrows who can reach a surface that has to exist and be correct first.
acceptance_criteria: The administrative routes are unreachable from outside the permitted network in a deployed environment, and docs/deployment.md states the precondition and how to configure it.
close_reason: Closed

title: Volunteer search matches only the display name, not the identifiers that disambiguate
description:
VolunteerSerializer carries email and slack_id with the reason stated in its docstring: two people called Sean are why the list is searched before anyone adds themselves, and without something to tell them apart the picker cannot help.

But VolunteerFilter.by_name searches display_name alone. A volunteer who types their own email address finds nobody and adds a duplicate -- the exact outcome the endpoint exists to prevent, arrived at through the field that was added to prevent it.

Widening the filter to email and slack_id is a few lines. Worth deciding at the same time whether the picker should search them, or only display them once a name match is found, since an email is not what somebody types when looking for themselves in a list.

Found by a review of inventory-tng-hd0.
acceptance_criteria: Searching by an identifier the serializer exposes finds the volunteer holding it, or a decision records why only names are searched.
close_reason: Closed

title: What active=False means for stock that is still on the shelf
description:
Item.active and Location.active retire a row without deleting its ledger history. Nothing says what that means for stock the retired row still holds, and the two halves of the API now answer differently by omission:

READ. /api/items and /api/locations both hide inactive rows, matching the volunteer pick-list. So a volunteer cannot see, and therefore cannot count or move, stock that is physically on a shelf under a retired item or in a decommissioned room.

WRITE. POST /api/stock/transactions filters the actor to a selectable volunteer but accepts any item, from_location and to_location. So a retired item CAN be recorded against -- just not found through the read API -- and it then reappears in the inventory_stock_balance view with a non-zero quantity.

The asymmetry needs deciding rather than assuming, and the two directions are not the same question: draining an inactive location while decommissioning it is legitimate, moving stock INTO one is not. A retired item is probably never a legitimate target either way, but its remaining stock still has to be countable off the shelf.

Raised by reviews of inventory-tng-hgm and inventory-tng-eg8.
acceptance_criteria: A decision is recorded about what active=False means for reading and for writing, and both halves of the API match it. If retired rows need to be reachable for a stock count, the read API offers a way that is not a guess.
close_reason: Decision 0019: retirement takes a row out of the pick-list and says nothing about its stock. Stock may leave a retired location and may not arrive, enforced by trigger; the read half was already ?withdrawn=true.

title: Batch validation resolves item and location one query per line
description:
StockMovementInputSerializer resolves item, from_location and to_location through PrimaryKeyRelatedField, whose to_internal_value does get(pk=...) per value. A 24-line transfer therefore costs up to 72 sequential SELECTs before a single row is written, and MAX_MOVEMENTS=500 admits up to 1500 -- against a request whose actual write is two statements. A real cart repeats the same handful of items and one or two locations, so nearly all of them are duplicates of each other.

This is the endpoint the project exists for, and it is used from a phone whose connectivity where stock is kept is unmeasured (ADR 0011 context), so latency here is worth caring about.

Two shapes: resolve in bulk in StockTransactionCreateSerializer.validate (collect every item and location id across the lines, two filter(pk__in=...) queries, report unknown ids by index through the existing error envelope, build movements with item_id=/from_location_id=); or a smaller PrimaryKeyRelatedField subclass memoising lookups across the batch, which collapses 3N to one per distinct id for much less change.

Raised by a review of inventory-tng-hgm; not done there because it restructures validation and its error reporting.
acceptance_criteria: Posting a batch of N lines over M distinct items and locations issues a number of validation queries proportional to M, not N. Unknown ids are still reported by line index. Existing endpoint tests pass unchanged.
close_reason: TLS is no longer a chart toggle and rendering without a certificate fails; batch validation now resolves each distinct id once, taking a 24-line cart from 81 queries to 12

title: API rules with no database counterpart
description:
Several rules the API enforces mirror no database constraint, so anything writing past the serializers and views -- the admin, a fixture load, the planned sheet importer -- is not held to them.

1. The kind-to-sides rule. KIND_SIDES in backend/src/inventory/views.py says which sides each movement kind must carry and which it must not: a checkout needs a from_location, a receipt needs a to_location and must NOT carry a from_location, consumption must not carry a to_location, a transfer needs both (ADR 0011 section 6). Every other per-line rule the serializer reports mirrors a real CheckConstraint. This one mirrors nothing, so another writer can record a receipt that drains a warehouse, and the ledger is append-only so it stands until somebody compensates it.
